references.text: The parallel text in [ref:Matt 21:7|Matthew 21:7] describes the same event where the disciples laid their cloaks on the donkey and let Jesus sit on it. Matthew mentions both the donkey and the colt.
The parallel text in [ref:Mark 11:7|Mark 11:7] tells of the same thing: they brought the colt to Jesus, laid their cloaks on it, and he sat on it.
In [ref:Joh 12:14-15|John 12:14-15], the same event is described where Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, with reference to the prophecy in Zechariah.

The prophecy in [ref:Sak 9:9|Zechariah 9:9] predicts that the king of Zion shall come riding on a donkey, on a colt. Luke's account of Jesus being placed on the colt is a fulfillment of this messianic prophecy.

In [ref:2 Kong 9:13|2 Kings 9:13], the people laid their cloaks under Jehu when he was proclaimed king. The fact that the disciples laid their cloaks on the colt for Jesus reflects this royal custom and acknowledges Jesus as king.
